Life2.0

What if you could live your life all over again?

A complete life, from the womb to old age, lived in one sitting. You decide how hard to try, where to go and whom to trust. Chance decides the rest. When it ends you see its shape, and you may live it again in the same world.

A session in four steps

  1. 01
    Settle into the chair.

    Your body rests. A simulated lifetime unfolds around you.

  2. 02
    Choose your starting conditions.

    Random by default, or a body profile, an upbringing and ten starting points.

  3. 03
    Live, and read the turns.

    Childhood plays by itself. From ten you set your effort and face decisions.

  4. 04
    Return and look back.

    Where you lived, what it cost, what it taught. Then try another path.

Three things keep a person alive

  • BodyPhysical health. When it fails, the life ends.
  • MindReasoning and emotional skill, built by practice.
  • ContentmentIkigai. Low contentment wears down the body and the mind.

At the end you receive a route map of where you lived, your Ikigai in four readings, and the lessons your choices taught.

Every number is an authored game rule. Not a psychological test, a forecast, or medical or financial advice.

How it works

Choices compound. Chance interrupts.

A life runs on one clock. You can pause it, slow it or speed it up; it never runs backwards.

A life, stage by stage

0–10 · Childhood
Your family decides. Each year is a short chapter about care, school and money at home. Some city children grow up with grandparents in the provinces.
From 10 · Effort
Spread ten points across body, reasoning, emotional skill, creativity and drive. Revisit them every five years.
From 15 · Money
Your own account, separate from your family's. Everyday living takes most of what you earn; what you save becomes your runway.
From 20 · Routes and places
College and a field of study, work, a trade or your own venture. Move to Bangkok, the provinces, Singapore, Tokyo, Boston or London, and back.
Decisions
Love, marriage, children, a hard boss, a loan, a funeral abroad. The gravest stop time until you choose. Many return years later.
The end
It may come early. Nothing guarantees eighty. Then you may live again in the same world, under the same storms.

Session

Time
2×, 3×, 10× or 20×. Childhood plays by itself; each later chapter is five years.
Reading
Standard, large or extra-large text. Reduced motion keeps every event but removes animation.
Languages
English, Thai, Simplified Chinese, Japanese and Korean, switchable at any time.
Sound
Original music, Small Hours (CC0), off until you start it.
Devices
Phone, tablet or computer. No download, no account.
Saving
Your life is stored only in this browser. Starting a new life replaces it; your last life is kept for comparison.

Conditions

You did not earn your starting line

Random is the default, because that is how birth works. You may set three conditions instead. None of them decides your worth or your outcome.

Choose conditions →

If you feel unsafe, reach someone you trust today. In Thailand, the mental health hotline is 1323.

Starting conditions

Body profile
Female, male or intersex. It changes how you look, not what you can become.
Upbringing
Constrained, middle or comfortable household money. It sets family support, school and where you are born.
Birthplaces
Khlong Toei riverside community · an Isan rice village · a Bang Na apartment block · a Pak Phanang fishing town · Samut Prakan · a walled house on Sukhumvit.
Households
Two parents, a parent and a grandmother, two mothers or two fathers. Stated at birth.
Starting shape
Ten points across five attributes. A game constraint, not a biological law: practice changes what you can do.
Later places
Singapore · Tokyo · Somerville, Massachusetts · London. Pay and living costs change with the place.

Care & consent

Difficult themes
Bereavement, illness, debt, a hard marriage, losing work, depression. Every branch keeps recovery possible.
No verdicts
No score for a good life. Marrying or not, children or not, staying or leaving are all valid; the game shows what each opened and closed.
Your data
No account, no analytics, no backend. Your life never leaves this browser. Clearing site data deletes it.
Money
Amounts are game rules in baht. They are not financial advice.
Health
Effects are authored. No medically specific odds, no drug benefits.
Bodies and minds
IQ and EQ are game indices, not tests. Inborn traits never decide a career.

The record

What you take home

When a life ends, the session returns a record built only from what happened. Nothing is invented to fill it.

What the record shows

Route map
One line per place you lived, your path in amber, moves as interchanges, with study, love, loss and coming home marked.
Ikigai
Four readings: what you love, what you practised, what the world got from you, and whether income covered your costs. Money alone cannot fill it.
Body, mind, money
Health, wellbeing and personal net worth across your ages, with the fastest change marked.
What it cost later
Each past choice that came back, with its age and amount.
Lessons
What each decision was teaching, linked to the essay it came from.
Runway
How many months you could have lived without income at 60.

Research

The neighbourhood
Metaphorical. Nearby buildings represent parts of a life, not a real map.
Inheritance
Inherited differences and environments interact. Heritability describes population variation, not an unchangeable percentage of a person. Deary et al. · Pinker, The Blank Slate
Personality
Big Five traits, reasoning, emotional skills and empathy are distinct, and personality can change. Stieger et al.
Lessons
Twenty-three decisions come from the author's essays at nonharvard.wordpress.com.
Universe 25
An enclosed-mouse experiment, not proof that prosperity causes extinction. Calhoun
Prior art
Content of 1in8b.life audited for comparison. Health and work interruptions are authored scenarios, not clinical predictions. WHO: Dengue · WHO: HIV
